name: Benjamin
description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: She named him Ben-oni, son of my sorrow, with her last breath, and Jacob called him Benjamin, son of the right hand: he did not let her dying emotion name his son.

note.label: Restoring the Broken Minds of the Daughters of Zion

points: Jacob sent not Benjamin with his brethren; lest peradventure means perhaps mischief befall him. Benjamin was the youngest boy, and he was Rachel's son: Rachel died in hard labour bearing him, calling him Benoni as her soul was departing, but his father called him Benjamin.

Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and Rachel was barren for years; she brought forth only Joseph and Benjamin. With Joseph presumed dead, Benjamin was the last son Jacob had of his beloved wife, so he would not let him go down.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

points: Every man's bundle of money was in his sack, and they were afraid; and Jacob their father said, me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

points: Joseph lifted up his eyes and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, God be gracious unto thee, my son. His bowels did yearn upon his brother, and he entered into his chamber and wept there; then he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself.

note.label: Genesis 43: Benjamin Brought Down to Egypt

points: Benjamin's mess was five times so much as any of theirs. Joseph gave all of them provision, but he made sure his baby brother was well taken care of: Benjamin was his mother's son and had nothing to do with him being sold. And they drank, and were merry with him.

note.label: Genesis 43: Benjamin Brought Down to Egypt

points: The steward searched, beginning at the eldest and leaving at the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack; they rent their clothes and returned to the city. Benjamin found with the cup gave Joseph cause to hold him, and it set the stage for Judah to speak the whole history.

note.label: Genesis 44: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and Judah's Surety

points: Benjamin is the so-called Jamaican today. Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: loud when he communicates, quick to anger, fierce; in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.
With Dan absorbed into him, Benjamin was dangerous in captivity; his slave revolts were plenty, and they were successful.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

points: Moses charged the people that day: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph (which is Ephraim and Manasseh), and Benjamin were to stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

points: And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him. Dwelling in safety means Benjamin would not be killed off in slavery.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

The victory belonged to the Most High, as he had promised.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

The men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, men of every city, and beast, and all that came to hand, and set on fire all the cities they came to.

Let him alone and let him curse, for the Most High hath bidden him. It may be that the Most High will look on his affliction and requite him good for the cursing this day.

David reasoned that if his own son sought his life, this Benjamite was nothing; the Most High was doing this, so let him curse. It may be the Most High will look on all that was done to David and bless him in front of them, the same as when people try to bring us down and the Most High blesses us before them, which is why this congregation has grown exponentially.
